topic: Why your stomach doesn't digest itself

sources.title: Your stomach juices are so acidic they can digest zinc

claims.text: IFLScience reports gastric juice can dissolve zinc.
claims.quote: Your gastric juice is capable of dissolving your organs, zinc, and the legs of living frogs

claims.text: Gastric acid's pH is between about one and three.
claims.quote: In humans, the pH of gastric acid is between one and three; generally sitting around 1.5 and 3.5 on the pH scale

claims.text: An adult stomach secretes about 1.5 litres of gastric juice a day.
claims.quote: A typical adult human stomach will secrete about 1.5 liters of gastric juice daily

claims.text: The lining secretes thick mucus with bicarbonate, which protects it from digesting itself.
claims.quote: This mucus, along with bicarbonate, forms a protective layer that prevents the stomach from digesting itself; secretes a thick alkaline mucus, rich in bicarbonate

claims.text: The epithelial cells of the lining are tightly joined together, part of the barrier.
claims.quote: the epithelial cells themselves, which are tightly joined together
